subject: physics_2
question_text: What do you understand by the terms 'node' and 'antinode'?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. The two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE for this paper: the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers, so neither check was run. Physics hand-checked: in a stationary wave y = 2A sin kx cos ωt, the amplitude 2A sin kx is zero at kx = 0, π, 2π … (nodes) and maximum at kx = π/2, 3π/2 … (antinodes); nodes and antinodes are fixed positions, alternating λ/4 apart.

recall_prompt: Say what a node is and what an antinode is, in a stationary wave.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Node
lines: In a stationary wave, the points where the
displacement of the particles is always
steps.margin_note: First mark. The word always matters — a node never moves, at any instant.
steps.why: In a stationary wave the amplitude 2A sin kx depends on position; where sin kx = 0 the particle can never move — those fixed positions are the nodes.
common_mistakes: Saying the displacement is zero at some instant — every particle passes through zero twice a cycle. A node has zero displacement at ALL times.
Placing nodes in a progressive wave — nodes and antinodes exist only in stationary waves.

recall.must_convey: That a node is a point of a stationary wave where the displacement is always zero.
accept: the particle never moves at a node
amplitude is zero at a node

steps.memory_tip: Node — no motion. The n of node is the n of no.

steps.label: Antinode
lines: The points where the particles vibrate
Nodes and antinodes alternate along the
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Anti = opposite: the antinode is the opposite of the node — maximum vibration.
steps.why: Where sin kx = ±1 the amplitude takes its largest value 2A — those positions vibrate the most, exactly midway between the nodes.
common_mistakes: Saying an antinode is at maximum displacement at all times — it vibrates THROUGH zero; its amplitude, not its position, is the maximum.
Writing the node–antinode gap as λ/2 — that is node to node. Node to the next antinode is λ/4.

recall.must_convey: That an antinode is a point of a stationary wave where the particles vibrate with maximum amplitude.
accept: amplitude is maximum at an antinode

steps.memory_tip: Anti means opposite — the antinode does the opposite of the node: it vibrates the most.

insider_note: The word always in the node definition is what separates a full mark from a half — every particle is momentarily at zero twice a cycle, but only a node stays there.
